name: Abdominal implants (six-pack implants)

card.summary: Surgical silicone implants placed over the abdominal wall to create the look of defined abs without building them through training.
card.note: Surgical procedure with operative risks; related technique abdominal etching is liposuction-based.

quick.overview:
Six-pack implants are shaped inserts placed in the abdominal wall to simulate the ridges of a rectus abdominis. The idea is to add definition for people who cannot or do not want to reveal it through diet and training.

A related technique, abdominal etching, removes fat selectively to sharpen existing muscle lines.
quick.how: A surgeon chooses the approach and sizing in consultation; the procedure is surgical and done in a clinic or hospital.
quick.risks: Surgical risks include pain, swelling, bruising, infection and shape irregularities. For liposuction-based etching, risks include numbness, scarring and rarely serious complications.

lead: Abdominal implants, or six-pack implants, are surgical inserts meant to create visible abdominal muscle definition. They are discussed alongside abdominal etching, a liposuction technique first described in 1993 that sharpens the linea alba, linea semilunaris and tendinous intersections through selective fat removal.[1]

Abdominal etching is considered part of high-definition liposculpture rather than weight loss. Common effects are pain, bruising, swelling lasting weeks to months, numbness and scarring, and body-shape irregularities in about 20% of patients; serious complications include thrombosis, fat embolism and organ perforation.[1]
T Nation members have discussed six-pack surgery and asymmetrical abs in threads from the 2000s.[2][3]

chain: Surgeon places implants or removes fat selectively
Ridges of the abdominal wall become visible
angle.text: The procedure creates or sharpens the look of a six-pack. Etching works best where muscle exists; implants add the shape.

paras: Fat is removed through a suction cannula; surgeons often combine techniques, with differential liposuction revealing muscle lines.[1] Reports note fat can return after a few months, mostly in the abdomen, with visceral fat linked to metabolic disease.[1]
Deaths from liposuction were reported at roughly one per 10,000 cases as of 2011, and the CDC reported deaths after cosmetic surgery abroad linked to embolism.[1]
T Nation includes a 2007 thread titled "NHE New Cool Six-Pack Surgery" and a 2009 thread on asymmetrical abs.[2][3]
No studies found on abdominal implants specifically.

timeline.event: Liposuction overtakes breast augmentation as the most common US cosmetic procedure.[1]
